sources.content: Iceland is an island country in the North Atlantic Ocean, and its mainland lies just south of the Arctic Circle. Its capital, Reykjavik, is the northernmost capital of a sovereign state, and about two thirds of the population live in or near it. The island sits on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge, where the North American and Eurasian plates move apart, so volcanoes and hot springs are common. Geothermal energy heats about nine in ten homes.

Iceland's parliament, the Althing, was founded in 930 and is one of the oldest parliaments in the world. The country became fully independent from Denmark in 1944, when it declared itself a republic. Iceland has no standing army, though it was a founding member of NATO in 1949. Its largest glacier, Vatnajokull, covers about 8 percent of the country. The currency is the Icelandic krona. Iceland joined the European Economic Area in 1994 but is not a member of the European Union.
